News.title: I’m a Croatia expert: These are the country’s most beautiful seaside destinations
News.content:
Croatia offers more than 1,100 miles of meandering mainland coast backed by rugged limestone mountains, along with hundreds of scattered islands and islets, of which 52 are inhabited. It is also dotted with historic and beautifully preserved harbour towns, relics of the four centuries between 1420 and 1797 when it was occupied by the Venetians. This combination makes it the perfect option for those who like to combine cultural sightseeing with lazing on the beach.

You’ll also find exhilarating water sports (sailing, scuba diving, sea kayaking and wind surfing) and land-based adventure activities (mountain biking, hiking and rock climbing), plus authentic local cuisine, showcasing the region’s Adriatic seafood, olive oil and wine.

Almost all of Croatia’s beaches are of pebble and rock – there’s very little sand. In some cases you swim from man-made concrete bathing platforms with steps into the sea. On the up side, this means limpid waters, with excellent visibility for snorkelling and scuba.

But where to go? Below is our guide to Croatia’s five coastal regions: South Dalmatia, Central Dalmatia, North Dalmatia, Kvarner and Istria. Within each region, two standout towns and one beach have been highlighted, along with a day-trip suggestion, food and wine suggestions, and hotel recommendations.

Sports.title: ‘Not a great team’ – Man Utd legend brands title-chasing Arsenal ‘boring’ in savage attack on Champions League finalists
Sports.content:
PAUL SCHOLES has branded Arsenal “boring” in a savage attack on the Premier League title chasers.

The Gunners are favourites for the title in what would end their 23-year wait to be champions of England.





Arsenal’s hopes were boosted as Everton held title rivals Manchester City to a 3-3 draw on Monday night.

Mikel Arteta‘s team could be on the brink of being champions if they beat West Ham on Sunday and the Cityzens fail to beat Brentford.

Scholes, 51, is not excited by the North London outfit becoming champions elect.

The Manchester United legend won the Premier League 11 times during his glittering career.

He played in iconic teams that boaste talent such as Eric Cantona, Cristiano Ronaldo and Wayne Rooney.

The retired midfielder has insisted that Arsenal’s failure to beat the likes of City, Liverpool and losing to United affects their ranking among the greats.

Scholes has also insisted that he would not turn on his TV to watch the Gunners, claiming they are “boring”.

Scholes salvaged the Gunners during an appearance on the latest episode of The Overlap‘s Stick to Football podcast.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He said: “I don’t think they’re the best champions we’ll ever see.

“I don’t think we’ll talk about this team in years to come like great United teams.

“You don’t always have to beat the top teams – they’ve not beat City and Liverpool, the best teams for the last four, five, six years.

“That’s why I don’t think people will speak about them being a great team.



“I know you can get away with not winning those games, of course you can, but to be a great team, you’ve got to go and beat these teams.

“They won’t have beaten City, won’t have beaten Liverpool, United beat them.

“You can win in all different ways, I’m just trying to say, they’re not a team I’d turn on and watch all the time.

“We’ve seen [David] Raya and the centre-halves just playing and playing.



“It’s been boring.”

Arsenal could get their hands on a historic double this season, having also reached the final of the Champions League.

They will face holders Paris Saint-Germain in the final in Budapest on May 30.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Scholes has been a vocal critic of the Gunners throughout the season.



In January, he claimed that only Bukayo Saka would have a chance of making it in a previous title-winning attack.

Sports.title: Manchester City stars lead transfer recommendations for Gameweek 35
Sports.content:
DREAM TEAM managers have until 11am on Saturday morning to confirm their transfers for Gameweek 35.

Manchester City and Crystal Palace are the only two teams scheduled to play twice with Pep Guardiola’s set to double up again in Gameweek 36, creating a clear focal point for gaffers to target.



MANCHESTER CITY’S REMAINING FIXTURES



GW35: Brentford (h) & Crystal Palace (h)

GW36: Chelsea (n) & Bournemouth (a)

GW37: Aston Villa (h)

Loading up on Etihad residents for the next two Gameweeks will be an immensely popular strategy but which players are best placed to capitalise?

There’s surely no need for us to bang the Jeremy Doku (£4.8m) drum again.

We singled the Belgian winger out as a potential difference maker in last week’s transfer recommendations and he immediately obliged with a 22-point mega haul.

His ownership has almost doubled in the last fortnight but it still looks relatively low at 11.7% given he’s the most in-form asset in Dream Team right now.

Antoine Semenyo (£4.6m) is among the most popular recruits ahead of Saturday’s deadline but his individual form has cooled in recent weeks.

The 43.6%-owned winger has racked up 282 points via 18 goals this season but has scored just once in his last ten outings.

The vast majority of Dream Team bosses will be piling into Man City with their latest transfers but one way to go against the grain would be to select an alternative to Semenyo.



The Ghana international is perfectly capable of punishing his doubters but it’s simply true that he has not been as effective as Doku or Rayan Cherki (£5m) at the business end of the campaign.

Speaking of the talented Frenchman, he has to be considered among the strongest options having banked 55 points over the last six Gameweeks.

Cherki has registered five assists, nine bonus points and a goal during this fruitful spell.

Only Bruno Fernandes (£6.9m) has provided more assists and created more big chances than City’s No10 this season.



Nico O’Reilly (£4.4m) has actually outscored Cherki over the last six Gameweeks but only by a single point.

Categorised as a midfielder in Dream Team, the England international has been more commonly used as a left-back but it doesn’t really matter as he takes up attacking positions in the penalty area no matter his designated role.

The 21-year-old has contributed nine goals and eight assists in all competitions this season.

Like Doku, O’Reilly’s ownership of 12.8% suddenly appears low with four fixtures to fulfil across the next two Gameweeks.

In defence, it remains mystifying that Matheus Nunes (£5.3m) features in just 5.9% of teams while Marc Guehi (£4.5m) is by far and away the most selected defender in the game (40.9%) given the Portuguese full-back has one more point to his name than the England centre-back.



The former is the only player in his position into double figures for assists (11) at this late stage of the campaign.

Gaffers tempted to switch David Raya (£4.3m) for Gigi Donnarumma (£4.4m) should note that James Trafford (£4.2m) is likely to start the FA Cup final in Gameweek 36.

If this proves true then the rangy Italian will only have one additional fixture over Arsenal’s No1 across the next two Gameweeks.

Furthermore, the Gunners will feel confident of clean sheets against West Ham (a) and Burnley (h) in their next two league games as they strive to claim their first title since 2004.



All things considered, trading Raya for Donnarumma seems like a waste of a transfer that could be put to better use elsewhere.

What about Crystal Palace?

The Eagles will host Everton before travelling to the Etihad but the appeal of their double header is negated by their European adventures.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Oliver Glasner’s side are expected to book their place in the Conference League final later today when Shakhtar Donetsk rock up at Selhurst Park as the hosts hold a 3-1 aggregate lead from the first leg.

If that’s the case then Dream Team bosses should expect reduced league minutes from the likes of Daniel Munoz (£5.2m) and Ismaila Sarr (£4.6m) in Gameweek 35, as was the case last weekend.

Sports.title: Mass riots erupt in Paris after PSG secure Champions League final spot with flaming bins hurled at cops and 127 arrests
Sports.content:
MASS riots erupted across Paris after PSG secured a spot in the UEFA Champions League final against Arsenal.

Footage circulating on social media shows the chaos breaking out in the heart of the French capital, not long after the semi-final win over Bayern Munich.





Fans aimed directly for police deployed to protect the city – unleashing fireworks at them, setting fire to bins, and attacking vehicles, including a police car.

The worst scenes of violence saw gangs of youths taking part in running battles with the forces of law and order, as they tried to prevent looting.

Wearing hoodies and masks, young men clashed with the riot squads, who used tear gas and baton charges to repel them.

Interior Minister Laurent Nunez told CNews radio channel that “hundreds” of people wanted to “attack the police and also tried to loot businesses.”



He confirmed that 34 people, including 23 officers, have been injured and one of them is in serious condition after a “mortar” was launched at them.

“I strongly condemn these excesses which sadly become commonplace on nights when PSG wins,” Nunez said, also praising the performance of the police.



“We don’t get used to this. I condemn this extremely strongly. You always have hundreds of people creating these disturbances at the end of the festivities and even during them.

He added: “To my knowledge, there was no looting of shops. There was an attempt, but it was prevented.

“The outcome was 127 arrests in the Paris metropolitan area, including 107 in Paris itself.



“And 11 people were injured, one seriously after using a mortar, and among the police officers, 23 sustained minor injuries.”

Police had shut Champs-Élysées, the avenue football fans normally head to after famous victories – but this did not stop large numbers congregating in other areas.

Another police spokesperson in the north of the city said: “They tried to block the ring road, but they were prevented from doing so.”



The UEFA final between PSG and Arsenal has been scheduled on May 30 at the Puskas Arena in Budapest, Hungary.

Nunez admitted that on the night, there will be a risk of disturbances, and added: “There will be the same firm response as last night.

“We can celebrate a sporting event, but there are always a few hundred individuals who come to cause trouble, and they will always receive a very firm response from the State.”

Paris has been plagued by football violence after major PSG fixtures in recent years.

Fears are mounting whether there will be a repeat of 2025’s violence that turned deadly.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

In May 2025, there were two fatalities linked to PSG unrest – a 17-year-old boy who died after he was reportedly stabbed in the chest, and a man, 23, who was riding a scooter and was hit by a car.

The interior ministry said 18 police officers in Paris had been injured, along with three elsewhere in France, as were 192 fans in the streets.

Sports.title: Tottenham manager Roberto de Zerbi labelled an ‘a**hole’ by former Premier League rival after training bust-up
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM boss Roberto De Zerbi has been blasted as an “a**hole” by former Premier League rival Jesse Marsch after a training-ground bust-up with midfielder Ismael Kone.

Marsch, now manager of Canada, launched the astonishing attack while defending international star Kone following his difficult spell under De Zerbi at Marseille.





The Italian only recently arrived at Spurs but is already a controversial figure after dividing opinion during his time in France.

De Zerbi faced backlash last year for publicly backing ex-Manchester United forward Mason Greenwood following his move to Marseille.

Greenwood joined the French side in 2024, two years after he was arrested on suspicion of rape, assault and coercive and controlling behaviour.

The Crown Prosecution Service later dropped all charges after key witnesses withdrew and new material came to light.

Greenwood denied the allegations throughout.

De Zerbi described Greenwood as a “good guy” during his time at Marseille before later insisting he “never wanted to downplay the issue of violence against women”.

But another flashpoint came when explosive footage emerged of De Zerbi furiously confronting Kone during a training session.

The clip showed the Marseille boss raging after the midfielder lost possession in a drill.

An angry De Zerbi shouted: “Oh my god, when I say reduce the touches, reduce the touches.”

He then appeared to throw Kone out of training, yelling: “I can’t play, go get a shower. Go get a shower Isma, we are Olympique Marseille.”



As Kone walked away, De Zerbi continued shouting: “Call your agent, call your agent,” before coaching staff and players stepped in to separate the pair.

Speaking later in a documentary, De Zerbi questioned whether Kone was mentally ready to play for Marseille despite praising his talent.

He said: “He is one of the players with the most potential at Olympique Marseille, but who didn’t always behave well.”

Marsch has now hit back in defence of the midfielder, insisting the Canadian international was badly treated by the current Spurs boss.

He said: “It wasn’t easy for him with De Zerbi in Marseille. De Zerbi was a real a**hole to him, but he stayed strong.



“He never doubted himself. He found a new environment, and look at him thriving today. I repeat: De Zerbi behaved like a real a**hole to him.”

Marsch also praised Kone’s professionalism and development, revealing he has worked closely with the midfielder on discipline, diet, sleep and concentration since taking over Canada.

Sports.title: Man Utd chief quietly LEAVES club two years after joining Sir Jim Ratcliffe following takeover
Sports.content:
SIR JIM RATCLIFFE’S right-hand man, Sir Dave Brailsford, has left his role as a director at Manchester United.

The news was quietly made in a Companies House Manchester United Football Club Limited filing on May 7.





The statement confirmed the termination of Brailsford’s time as a director on April 30.

Brailsford, 62, joined the club as a director after the partial takeover of Ineos in February 2024.

The former head of British cycling played a major role in the restructuring of the club’s hierarchy, including the hiring of current CEO Omar Berrada, and was in charge of football operations for more than a year.

His duties at the club were scaled back last year following United’s disappointing season as the club went trophyless and finished a record low 15th place in the Premier League under Ruben Amorim.

But Brailsford has now completely left his duties at United.

Despite this change, the “marginal gains” philosopher remains a close advisor to United’s British billionaire owner and is continuing in his role as director of sport with Ineos.

He returned to the Ineos Grenadiers cycling team last June with the aim of landing an eighth Tour de France title for the team, having previously stood down when Ratcliffe purchased his minority stake in the Red Devils.

The Times report two senior Ineos figures will now join the club’s board.

Brailsford oversaw the success of Team Sky, later Team Ineos, in the Tour de France with six out of seven victories in the prestigious competition between 2012 and 2018, only failing to win in 2014.

His efforts saw the likes of British sporting icons Bradley Wiggins, Chris Froome and Geraint Thomas all claim Tour de France titles.

Before that Brailsford had led Team GB cycling at the Olympics and beyond.

Britain led the cycling medal table at the 2008 and 2012 Olympic Games with eight golds at both, while British cyclists won a whopping 59 World Championship titles across different disciplines between 2003 and 2013.

While at United he launched Mission 21 – the aim of a 21st league title for the men’s team – and Mission 1 – the aim of a first league title for the women’s team – as part of the wider Project 150 to rebuild the club to its former glory before it’s 150th birthday in 2028.



The goal is to ultimately see United win a Premier League by then again, while it is hoped the women’s team can land their inaugural WSL title.

Key figures such as nutritionist James Morton were brought in to overhaul the way the club was run on and off the pitch, including the £50million redevelopment of the club’s Carrington training facility.

Sports.title: Arsenal stars set for staggering bonuses if they win historic Premier League and Champions League Double
Sports.content:
ARSENAL stars are targeting an astronomical bonus worth millions if they win a historic Premier League and Champions League Double.

The Gunners are only three league wins away from winning their first Prem title since the Invincibles’ campaign in 2004 after finishing as runners-up the last three seasons.





And the North Londoners punched their ticket to the Champions League final where they will face reigning European champions Paris Saint-Germain after eliminating Atletico Madrid in the semi-finals.

Mikel Arteta‘s men have more than just glory to play for as the aforementioned historic feat would also include a lucrative payday.

According to The Times, an Arsenal player who played every game and won both the Premier League as well as the Champions League would earn approximately £2.13million in bonuses.

Arteta’s stars would pocket a total of £1,175,000 if they become European champions on May 30 at the Puskas Arena in Budapest.

That would include a fee of £125,000 for winning the final and £50,000 they made from the semi-finals.

Arsenal stars have also sealed an approximate £1m bonus for qualifying for the competition after finishing second in the league last season.

Then there’s a bonus worth a total of £228,000 across a 38-game Premier League season.

That is based on nearly £6,000 per appearance for each Arsenal player.

And finally there’s an estimated shared bonus pool worth £725,000 per player.

That is accrued during progress in league and cup competitions, distributed based on appearances.

Arsenal have two more away matches in the league at West Ham and Crystal Palace, where they will play their final fixture of the season.

And there is one final home match on May 18 against relegated Burnley.

Sports.title: Man Utd at centre of ticket chaos with players’ families scrambling to attend FA Youth Cup final against City
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED players’ families are facing a scramble to get tickets for the FA Youth Cup final against arch rivals City.

The match was expected to be hosted at the 53,400-capacity Etihad, but will instead be played at the 7,000-seater Joie Stadium at City’s training ground.





A miniature away allocation of just 968 tickets for the relocated final has resulted in a severe shortage for United fans.

A United supporter group has written to FA chief executive Mark Bullingham asking him to “personally intervene” to switch the Youth Cup final venue.

Manchester United Supporters Trust (MUST) and Manchester United Fans’ Forum called the decision to move the 14 May final “a disgrace” in a joint statement.

While 67,000 fans packed into Old Trafford for United’s Youth Cup triumph in 2022, hundreds will cram into the 7,000-capacity stadium that usually hosts women’s and academy football.



There was a race against time with tickets priced at £5 for adults, while £3 concessions were made for Under-21s, Over-65s and wheelchair users.

The limited allocations means they will not be able to accept all the requests from players’ families for tickets.

Loyal academy supporters who regularly travel to Leigh Sports Village have been shut out of the allocation, losing out to season ticket holders and executive club members.

Typically, the Youth Cup final is held at the host club’s first-team stadium, and anticipation was high for the first all-Manchester event since 1984 in front of a potential 50,000 crowd.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

United sources feel it will cost the majority of the players involved an experience in what could turn out to be the biggest game of their lives.

The dad of United prodigy JJ Gabriel fumed on X, saying it is a “robbery of kids’ dreams”.

City were drawn at home for the match but are unable to use the main pitch, with Pep Guardiola‘s side still having three home Premier League games to play.

Construction work on the new stand at the Etihad was a complicating factor, with the club keen to host the final Prem home game against Villa and run a test event on May 20.



Since the turn of the century every host finalist has held the match at their first-team stadium – except for City.

City have made the final six times and hosted it at their Joie Stadium by the club’s training ground complex on five occasions.

But two years ago a crowd of 20,000 watched City beat Leeds United in the final at Etihad Stadium.

The FA is unlikely to step in as City have had clearance, but the governing body were supportive of City agreeing to move it to Old Trafford.

Delivery of the Youth Cup final is traditionally managed by the finalist club drawn first in the draw, and City did not want to give up home advantage.



SunSport has reached out to City for comment.

City, who also pipped United to the U18s league, beat Fulham, Arsenal, Chelsea, Everton and Blackburn en route to the final.

United secured their place after they overcame Peterborough United, Derby County, Oxford United, Sunderland and Crystal Palace.

Sports.title: Scottish club suspend manager as investigation launched and statement issued
Sports.content:
Scottish club suspend manager as investigation launched and statement issued

Elgin City have confirmed they have suspended manager Allan Hale with immediate effect, with the SPFL club announcing an ongoing investigation into the Highlanders boss

View 2 Images Allan Hale has been suspended from his role

Elgin City have suspended manager Allan Hale with immediate effect following the launch of an internal investigation into the boss.

‌



The Highlanders wrapped up the season in sixth place in League Two, Scottish football's bottom tier, following their final game of the season on Saturday.

‌



The Borough Briggs club have now dropped the bombshell in an official statement, which read: "Elgin City Football Club can confirm that the first team manager has been suspended from his duties with immediate effect, pending an ongoing investigation.

‌



"The club will make no further comment until the investigation has concluded."

Hale has been at the helm for two-and-a-half years, during which time he has played a significant role in strengthening the club.

The former Fraserburgh player was handed the Elgin City job in December 2023 when the club were embroiled in a relegation battle, reports the Daily Record.

‌



He departed Highland League side Huntly alongside his No. 2 Stefan Laird to take the reins at Elgin — and successfully steered them clear of the drop in his maiden season.

Hale went on to build real momentum at the club, guiding them into the play-offs in his first season, where they were beaten by Annan Athletic, before narrowly missing out on a repeat this campaign.

View 2 Images Elgin City play at Borough Briggs (Image: SNS Group)

‌



Elgin finished sixth in League Two, having taken 44 points from their 26 games with 11 wins, 11 draws and 14 defeats. They finished the campaign on a run of five games without a win following a final-day 1-0 defeat by Stranraer.

“We read the narrative about the club being in League 2 for 27 years and people looking at that as a negative,” Hale said on the weekend. “For me I don't think that's a negative at all. I actually think it says a lot about the resilience of the football club.

“If you look at Elgin it's geographically one of the most difficult teams to manage in Scottish football.

Sports.title: New Arsenal documentary gives fans fresh insight into Invincibles season as club eyes glory again
Sports.content:
New Arsenal documentary gives fans fresh insight into Invincibles season as club eyes glory again

Arsenal are on the verge of winning their first Premier League title in over two decades, Arsene Wenger's Invincibles the last north London side to achieve the feat

View Image Arsenal last won the Premier League in 2003/04 (Image: Getty)

All Out Football have launched a brand-new mini documentary exploring Arsenal's famed Invincibles season of 2003/04. It's been a lengthy wait of more than two decades since the Gunners last saw success in the Premier League.

‌



Arsene Wenger guided the club to the title in style in May 2004, having gone the entirety of the season unbeaten with 26 wins and 12 draws. And while Mikel Arteta has come increasingly close to guiding Arsenal to the prestigious piece of silverware since his arrival in 2019, it has been a case of always the bridesmaid but never the bride for the Spaniard thus far.

‌



The Gunners fell just five points shy of Manchester City in 2022/23, missed out to the same club by two points the following season, and were pipped to the post by Arne Slot's Liverpool by 10 last time round. However, that all appears poised to change this month. Arsenal sit five points clear of City at the summit of the league table with just three games to go, meaning that perfect performances against West Ham United, Burnley and Crystal Palace will see them reunited with the title after 22 long years.

‌



And in anticipation, All Out Football has launched a brand new mini documentary which looks into Arsenal's coveted campaign from 2003/04, as the Gunners look to end more than two decades of hurt in north London. You can check it out below...

Sports.title: Sir Dave Brailsford officially leaves Man Utd role after major INEOS reshuffle
Sports.content:
Sir Dave Brailsford officially leaves Man Utd role after major INEOS reshuffle

Sir Dave Brailsford is no longer involved at Manchester United, with the former cycling chief moving across to a different area of INEOS' business following a reshuffle

View 2 Images Sir Dave Brailsford is no longer involved at Manchester United (Image: PA)

Sir Dave Brailsford is no longer a part of the Manchester United hierarchy. The former Team Sky cycling chief was a part of the senior team at United following their takeover by INEOS, but has officially stepped back from the role.

‌



Sir Jim Ratcliffe installed Brailsford at United following his purchase of a stake in the club in December 2023. The 62-year-old was involved in setting up the new leadership team behind the scenes at Old Trafford, including the hiring of Omar Berrada as chief executive.

‌



But club filings reveal that Brailsford is no longer listed as a director, with his resignation officially dated on April 30. The Times reports that two other INEOS figures will now join the board. It follows reports from last summer that stated he would move back to his director of sport role for INEOS, who remain committed to cycling, which is Brailsford's area of expertise.

‌



Despite having no background in football, Brailsford spent a year in charge of football operations at United after INEOS took over control of the club from the Glazer family. His time in the position did not go well, with United finishing 15th in the Premier League last season and losing the Europa League final.

It was decided last summer that Brailsford would step away from United to return his focus to INEOS' cycling arm, as well as overseeing their ownership of Ligue 1 side Nice. He was previously team principal of Ineos Grenadiers.

‌



United are now run by Berrada, who was poached from Manchester City by INEOS to become chief executive, and Jason Wilcox, who is technical director. Things have taken an upturn since the duo decided to sack Ruben Amorim as manager in January, with interim boss Michael Carrick winning 10 of his 14 games in charge.

The club have secured a return to the Champions League for next season and sit third in the Premier League with three games remaining.

View 2 Images Sir Dave Brailsford with Jason Wilcox watching Manchester United's defeat in the Europa League final last May (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

‌



Although he oversaw improvements at the training ground, Brailsford's time at United will be remembered primarily for the brutal cuts made after Ratcliffe poured his money into the club. Hundreds of employees lost their jobs, while expenditure was slashed across many areas of the business.

That pattern has been seen elsewhere across INEOS' sport division, with funding removed from sailing and a sponsorship of the All Blacks.

Despite criticism, Ratcliffe openly championed the cuts at United, believing them to be necessary in order to return United to the top echelons of world football. "Manchester United has become mediocre," he told the United We Stand fanzine.

Article continues below

"It is supposed to be one of the best football clubs in the world. We have to make some difficult and unpopular decisions. If you shy away from the difficult decisions, then nothing much is going to change.”

Sports.content:
Liverpool issue statement and confirm massive U-turn after angry supporter backlash

Liverpool supporters have protested against owners Fenway Sports Group and proposed ticket price increases for the next three seasons during recent matches at Anfield

View 2 Images Liverpool fans have protested against proposed ticket price increases (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

Liverpool have backed down on plans to increase ticket prices for the next three seasons after protests by their supporters. Recent matches at Anfield have seen organised protests, with fans holding up banners and placards and chanting against their American owners - and a U-turn has now been announced.

‌



The club had previously announced fixed ticket price increases for the next three campaigns, sparking anger in the fanbase. Liverpool said inflation and a rise in operating costs needed to be covered, but the backlash, organised by fan groups, was significant, with owners Fenway Sports Group targeted.

‌



Liverpool chiefs have since held talks with fan groups, including Spirit of Shankly and Spion Kop 1906, and made a partial reversal. Instead of increases in line with inflation for the next three seasons, the club has compromised by raising the general admission price by three per cent next year with a price freeze for the 2027/28 campaign.

‌



"The club and Supporters Board will use the certainty of these seasons to seek longer-term alternative solutions across the game and explore commercial ideas with the Supporters Board in an attempt to avoid future ticket price increases and address issues around affordability and accessibility for future generations," Liverpool said in a statement.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Jamie Carragher issues public apology to Luis Enrique as PSG boss responds on live TV READ MORE :

Liverpool told to repeat Newcastle raid as Arne Slot transfer should only be a 'back-up' READ MORE :

"LFC believes that, without wider progress on alternative solutions, future inflationary increases may still be required, including season 2028-29, and will continue to engage with its supporters. Both the club and the Supporters Board are committed to exploring a longer-term solution that works in the interests of all.

‌



"The club also remains committed to managing its cost challenges responsibly, giving advance notice to supporters and certainty to its own financial planning to remain competitive at the highest levels of football."

In a joint statement with other involved fan groups, Spirit of Shankly said: "We understand disappointment at next season’s increase in ticket prices will remain for some, but there will be none the season after and we want to assure fans we will continue talks with the club and do our best to find other ways to prevent future rises.

View 2 Images Fans held up cards in protest against the price increases at Anfield last month (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA)

‌



"Our matchday culture has also been top of the agenda recently and again, SOS, as part of the Supporters’ Board, will work to protect it. We would like to thank those at LFC who have listened to us and engaged with us, not all club hierarchies would have done the same. And we look forward to working with them to find future paths that benefit all.

"We also want to thank you for backing us, for helping with handing out leaflets, for protesting and making sure your voices were heard. We could not have reached this point without you."

Liverpool are fourth in the Premier League and are set to finish the 2025/26 campaign without any silverware. Arne Slot's side host Chelsea at Anfield in Saturday's early kick-off before final matches against Aston Villa and Brentford.

Sports.title: England face Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka issue after Arsenal reach Champions League final
Sports.content:
England face Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka issue after Arsenal reach Champions League final

Thomas Tuchel is expected to see his England preparations for the World Cup impacted by Arsenal reaching the Champions League final

View 2 Images Arsenal stars Bukayo Saka and Declan Rice look to have handed Thomas Tuchel an England dilemma (Image: (Photo by Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images))

Bukayo Saka and Declan Rice look set to miss the bulk of England's pre-World Cup training camp owing to Arsenal's involvement in the Champions League final. The Gunners are due to take on Paris Saint-Germain in Budapest on Saturday, May 30, with a place in European football's history books up for grabs.

‌



Fellow Gunners Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke, who have both received call-ups from Thomas Tuchel on several occasions this season, find themselves in a similar position. Captain Harry Kane, however, is anticipated to be available following Bayern Munich's exit at the hands of PSG.

‌



According to Sky Sports' Rob Dorsett, the Three Lions are scheduled to jet off to Miami for a warm-weather training camp on Monday, June 1 — less than 48 hours after the Champions League final.

‌



Arsenal transfer target Khvicha Kvaratskhelia sends Champions League final message to Gunners READ MORE :

The Arsenal contingent are expected to be granted a minimum of six days' rest, meaning they will sit out the friendly against New Zealand on Saturday, June 6 in Tampa Bay. Four days on in Orlando, England take on Costa Rica, with Rice, Saka, Eze and Madueke all potentially in contention to feature.

England then kick off their World Cup campaign the following Wednesday against Croatia. Group-stage matches with Ghana and Panama arrive in the following two weeks.

‌



Tuchel's side are favourites to qualify top of group L and thus set up a round of 32 clash, likely against one of Ecuador, Norway, Senegal, Saudi Arabia or DR Congo.

Sky broadcasts more than 1,400 live matches across the Premier League, EFL and more with at least 215 live from the top flight alongside Formula 1, darts and golf.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



The immediate priority for England and Tuchel is to prepare for the three scheduled group matches, but Arsenal's Champions League success means he won't have everyone at his disposal straight away. It also means Gunners players face a gruelling schedule over at least the next seven weeks.

Though downtime will be scarce, Arsenal's four England regulars - which could rise to six following recent performances from Ben White and Myles Lewis-Skelly - might arrive in the United States brimming with confidence, having secured the Champions League and Premier League title.

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta's Arsenal could end the season as Premier League winners and European champions

‌



Mikel Arteta's team are just four matches away from accomplishing that feat, with their showdown against PSG coming after league fixtures against West Ham United, Burnley and Crystal Palace.

Title challengers Manchester City currently trail Arsenal by five points. However, Pep Guardiola's outfit have four games remaining, with their fixture against Crystal Palace, initially scheduled for the Carabao Cup final weekend, set to take place next Tuesday.

Before that, City host Brentford at the Etihad Stadium this weekend, with Arsenal travelling to West Ham United the day after.

Saka and Rice are both anticipated to feature in London, with their minutes being carefully monitored across the final two fixtures.

Sports.title: Vincent Kompany accuses referee of U-turning on red card for PSG star - 'Ridiculous'
Sports.content:
Vincent Kompany accuses referee of U-turning on red card for PSG star - 'Ridiculous'

Bayern Munich's Champions League semi-final exit was marred by two controversial decisions in the second leg, as Paris Saint-Germain escaped a penalty and a red card

View 2 Images Vincent Kompany was left aggrieved (Image: Sebastian Widmann - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany has accused referee Joao Pinheiro of U-turning on a red card for Paris Saint-Germain star Nuno Mendes. Kompany's side lost 6-5 to PSG on aggregate, having only been able to manage a 1-1 draw in the second leg in Munich.

‌



But Bayern were left aggrieved over two high-profile decisions. While PSG avoided giving away a penalty thanks to a little-known exemption in the handball law, an earlier incident also irked Kompany.

‌



In the 29th minute, the ball struck the arm of Mendes as he cut out a Bayern attack. Pinheiro immediately blew his whistle and awarded a free-kick to Bayern.

‌



Kompany appealed vehemently on the sidelines and wanted Mendes to be shown a second yellow card, having been booked in the opening stages. But after seemingly communicating with his fourth official, the Portuguese referee reversed his decision. It was deemed that Bayern's Konrad Laimer had also handled the ball seconds earlier, so PSG got the free-kick instead.

WORLD CUP LEGENDS: The stars who lit up football's greatest tournament - Buy the Special Edition today

Thierry Henry sends Arsenal clear reality check as PSG book Champions League final place READ MORE :

PSG handball controversy explained after Bayern Munich and Harry Kane fury READ MORE :

Mendes was therefore able to stay on the pitch and eventually helped PSG reach the final in Budapest, where they'll face Arsenal. Kompany believes that had the PSG defender not already been on a yellow card, his fate would've been sealed.

‌



"I thought he was giving it and I felt he pulled out because he realised he'd already given him a yellow and he didn't want to send him off for that," Kompany, who also labelled the officiating 'ridiculous' during his press conference, told TNT Sports.

"He's turned it around to the other side. I've seen it on a few angles. I don't see Konrad Laimer touch the ball with his hand. They say he did. So I don't know."

Should Nuno Mendes have been sent off? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Nuno Mendes was on a yellow card when the ball hit his arm (Image: GSI/Icon Sport via Getty Images)

Meanwhile, ex-Bayern midfielder Michael Ballack claimed on DAZN: "This is a game-changing situation. It is the first time that the fourth official intervenes in such a scene.

"I had the feeling that they didn't want to give the yellow-red card. That's my feeling as a spectator. I say that quite frankly.

‌



"Sometimes you look for situations so as not to steer a game in a direction. I don't want to accuse him of anything, but the situation didn't allow him to make this decision like that."

Bayern are still on for the double this season, having already won the Bundesliga title. They'll play Stuttgart in the DFB Pokal final.

Sports.title: Harry Kane names his favourite for PSG vs Arsenal Champions League final
Sports.content:
Harry Kane names his favourite for PSG vs Arsenal Champions League final

Bayern Munich were knocked out of the Champions League in the semi-finals by Paris Saint-Germain and Harry Kane has assessed Arsenal's chances against the defending champions

View 2 Images Harry Kane gave his take on the upcoming final between Arsenal and PSG

Arsenal will face an uphill battle against Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League final, according to Harry Kane. PSG booked their place in the final on Wednesday night after a 1-1 draw with Bayern Munich saw the defending champions progress 6-5 on aggregate.

‌



Ousmane Dembele's early goal in Munich gave the away side a two-goal lead to defend and they did so impressively. Kane found the back of the net in added time, but it was too little too late for Bayern.

‌



PSG thrashed Inter Milan 5-0 in last year's showpiece in one of the most one-sided finals of all time. This time they will face an Arsenal side competing in their first Champions League final for 20 years.

‌



The Gunners topped the group stage and are unbeaten in all 14 matches in the competition this season, having conceded just six times. They saw Atletico Madrid 2-1 on aggregate to reach the final in Budapest on May 30 and will go in as underdogs, according to Kane.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"In my opinion, PSG are slightly favourites in the final," Kane told Sky Sports Germany.

Although he scored late on, Kane was not given many sights of goal on Wednesday night, with William Pacho and Marquinhos impressive in central defence. The England captain has now turned his focus elsewhere.

"It's tough. We had enough chances today to reach the final," Kane added. "Now my focus is on the DFB-Pokal final. We have the chance to win the double."

‌



PSG are aiming to become the first team to successfully defend their Champions League title since Real Madrid won three successive titles between 2016 and 2018. Manager Luis Enrique is expecting a tough game against Arsenal and his former team-mate Mikel Arteta.

View 2 Images PSG will aim to defend their title against Arsenal on May 30 (Image: Getty Images)

HAVE YOUR SAY! Who will win the Champions League final? Comment below.

‌



"I appreciate Mikelito Arteta!" he said when asked about their opponents. "We used to be team-mates when we were kids, he did a great job at Arsenal. It will be a difficult, hard game but we believe in our football style."

Asked about his side's performance against Bayern, Enrique said: "The character we showed against a team like Bayern is so positive. We're so happy to reach a second Champions League final in a row. It was very intense.

"Very difficult. They play football at the highest level. Both teams are similar, we love to press higher. We are very happy. In two days I'm going to celebrate my birthday. I'm very happy. We're in the next phase of the competition, the final of the Champions League. We want to give our supporters that kind of gift."

Sports.title: Hull vs Millwall: 'Sixth vs third... but this is NOT a predictable tie'
Sports.content:
It is sixth versus third in the first of our Championship play-off semi-finals, but it feels like a much closer battle than usual between Hull and Millwall.

Hull may have only forced their way back into the play-offs on the final day, while Millwall still had a shout for automatic promotion as they eventually finished third, but for most of the season these two were going toe to toe in and around the top six. The Tigers were above the Lions as recently as February.

And both sides have beaten the other on the road this season. Hull won at The Den in December, while Millwall prevailed at the MKM in March.

It is set to be a fascinating tie...

Hull vs Millwall schedule Semi-final first leg - MKM Stadium - Friday May 8, kick-off 8pm

Semi-final second leg - The Den - Monday May 11, kick-off 8pm

Final - Saturday May 23

Story of the match In 17 of last 20 seasons, the team finishing third has beaten the team finishing sixth in the Championship play-off semi-finals.

The last team to finish sixth and reach the final were Derby in 2019, and the last to be promoted were Blackpool in 2010.

The team finishing third have reached final in 13 of last 15 seasons – six have won promotion.

Millwall have never won a play-off game at second-tier level (D1 L5) – they are the only team (out of 42) to play at least three play-off games at this level and never win.

Millwall had the best away record in the Championship this season, taking 41 points and losing only 4 games.

Hull have won both previous Championship play-off campaigns – in 2008 and 2016.

Hull scored the fifth-most goals in the Championship this season (70) from the fifth-fewest shots (515).

'It is sixth vs third, but it's not a predictable tie'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Sky Sports Essential EFL podcast looks ahead to the Championship play-off semi-final.

Don Goodman on the Sky Sports Essential EFL podcast:

"The gap isn't as big as usual in terms of points, but also in terms of what these two teams are capable of when they are operating close to their best.

"Hull can score goals against anybody, they have a wonderful blend in attack with the players they have, and they will craft out chances.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Sky Bet Championship match between Hull City and Norwich City.

"It is sixth versus third, but I don't think we've got a predictable tie.

"But flip it on its head and they also concede a lot of chances and a lot of goals. That could be the differential between these two over two legs. Millwall are just a much more solid outfit without the ball.

"I think Millwall are going to be a force in these play-offs. I would just about back them to come through this tie, but I don't anticipate that it's going to be straightforward."

Andy Hinchcliffe on the Sky Sports Essential EFL podcast:

"For Millwall to finish third is pretty incredible. To be as consistent as they have in this league is extraordinary.

"Hull have overachieved. Their underlying stats tell you they should be down in the bottom five or six. But they are challenging for promotion.

"Millwall being at home in the second leg is an advantage. They go into the tie in better form, but Hull have the ability to win games you don't expect them to win. That's why they are here.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Sky Bet Championship match between Millwall and Oxford United.

"Millwall are set up to be defensively solid. They're not going to give much away, but they do have individuals. Hull have more individuals that can change the course of the game. They don't necessarily have to play well to win games.

"Millwall might be the better unit, but Hull have players that can hurt you. There are Hull players that can score goals in different ways. Lots of width, different threats. Millwall will be wary of that.

"With Hull's unpredictability I wouldn't be surprised if they got through. But over the course of two games, Millwall should have enough to make it to Wembley."

The key battle & the wildcard

Sky Sports EFL Editor Simeon Gholam:



Were it not for the injury that kept him out for several weeks at the back end of 2025, Oli McBurnie would have been in the running for Championship Player of the Season.

The 29-year-old returned to the EFL with a bang after a year in Spain, scoring 17 times and providing seven assists in just 32 starts for Hull. His two goals on the final day steered them into the play-offs.

He has also won the sixth most aerial duels in the Championship this season (148) and his tussle with Millwall defender Jake Cooper could prove key to who prevails in this tie.

Cooper is a Lions legend, he has been at the club since 2017 and was an unused sub when they won the League One play-off final at Wembley that year.

He has the second most aerial duels won this year in the league (271), and also has the sixth most clearances and fourth most headed clearances.

McBurnie scored as Hull won 3-1 at Millwall in December, while Cooper scored when Millwall were victorious by the same scoreline at Hull in March.

Away from that, there is also Femi Azeez. The Millwall winger has been one of the stars of the division. He was nominated for EFL Championship Player of the Season and named in the Sky Sports Championship Team of the Season.

He has provided the spark in attack so often for the Lions this season, and could be crucial here again.

Jakirovic: Play-offs are a completely different approach

Sergej Jakirovic will be aiming to use his previous play-off experience to take into the tie with Millwall.

The 49-year-old has previously managed Dinamo Zagreb in a two-legged affair to try and get them into the Champions League in 2024, beating Qarabag to reach the group stage.

"It's a completely different approach," Jakirovic said. "In the last round [of games of the season] you must win and still you might not be in the top six.

"I think it will be easier to play because you have 180 minutes. I have experience from Dinamo [Zagreb] when we had a play-off to reach the Champions League.

"You have to be very wise. It will not decide anything, the first game. There are no away goals. It's who will handle the pressure better.

"No matter this result on Friday, Monday will be everything. We will try to hide our minuses. It's not so easy because we know them, they know us.

"It depends who will be in the mood to play one-on-ones, to pass the players, to make successful crosses into the box, who will score their chances."

Lewie Coyle: It would be beyond my wildest dreams to captain Hull to the Premier League

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hull captain Lewie Coyle discusses what it would mean to lead the Tigers back to the Premier League after a decade.

Hull have twice been promoted to the Premier League via the play-offs; in 2007/08 - thanks to that Dean Windass goal - and in 2015/16 under Steve Bruce.

On both occasions, Lewie Coyle watched his hometown club triumph from across the way in Leeds, where he was on the books from 2004 to 2020.

Now, though, the defender is the Tigers' club captain. And after they pipped Wrexham and Derby to the final play-off place on the last day of the regular season, he has a dream at the forefront of his mind.

"I was a young boy - I call it 'the golden era', when Hull had that first success at Wembley. That's the stuff I dreamed of being able to do as a player myself," he says.

"I look back with fond memories. It's great for the city, it's great for everyone involved at the club and it's now time for me to put my stamp on things and really try and make it happen."

This comes just a year after Hull avoided relegation to League One on goal difference alone.

The 30-year-old knows more than most what it would mean to reach the top flight.

"It means everything to be club captain," he added. "It's something I'm very, very proud of. I don't take it for granted. I know that a football career is very short and this will all be over someday.

"To be able to proudly say I'm the club captain of my hometown club, it would just make it that bit sweeter if we go on and achieve that ultimate dream of getting this club back to the Premier League.

"In a nutshell, that would do for me. It would be beyond my wildest dreams, and if I can keep a little promise I made to someone a long time ago, it would make me very, very happy."

Alex Neil: We have no fear going into the play-offs

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alex Neil explains the mentality Millwall will be taking into their Championship play-off semi-final with Hull City.

Millwall boss Alex Neil says his side will lean on their impressive away record and approach the first leg with no fear at Hull.

"Play-off games are different because they’re essentially knockout matches," he told Sky Sports. "We’ve got two legs to try and get the result we need.

"Our away form has been the best in the division, so we’re hoping to get a positive result in the first leg and then bring it back to The Den. The key thing is making sure the occasion doesn’t get the better of you, that will be crucial for both teams.

"I think the biggest difference is that we now play without fear. I only had half a season last year, but even then our away form in the second half of the campaign was pretty good.

"This year we’ve had a full season playing that way. Whether we’re home or away, we approach games the same way. There’s no major change in style depending on the venue, and that consistency has helped us pick up some brilliant away results.

"We've managed that well throughout the end of the season. When you’re in a strong position, naturally there’s more expectation and scrutiny on both the team and myself. But I think we’ve handled that better and better as the season has gone on.

"We’ve had big away games at Middlesbrough and Ipswich and handled them brilliantly. We then had games we absolutely needed to win, like QPR and Stoke.

"Leicester was probably the one disappointment towards the end of the season, but then we still had a job to do against Oxford and we managed that too. From our perspective, we’ve got nothing to lose. It’s about attacking every game and giving our best, just as we’ve done all season."

Crama: We're going to get there to attack

Millwall defender Tristan Crama insists they are going to the MKM Stadium to win the first leg.

"We know it's two games, but we're just focusing on Friday first," he told Sky Sports. "We had such a good record away this season, so we're going there to attack the game and win it. Obviously, it will only be halfway through it, but I'm not going to think about Monday first. I just think about Friday.

"We're just going to go there to attack and win it. We're not going there to try and hold a score. We did that all season, and we got the best away record. I'm going there to win the game.

"Every game is different, but [winning 3-1 at Hull in March] just means you go in there and you know you can beat them because you already did it.

"It's different now because it's the play-offs, so I guess the atmosphere at the stadium will be different as well. I'm looking forward to it.

"The mentality in the squad is amazing. We're not getting too low, we're not getting too high, so we still have the same mindset that we're going to attack the game like we attacked the previous 46 games."

Hull vs Millwall - Friday May 8, kick-off 8pm

Middlesbrough vs Southampton - Saturday May 9, kick-off 12.30pm

Play-off semi-final second legs

Millwall vs Hull - Monday May 11, 8pm

Sports.title: Jan Brueghel and Illinois clash in Ormonde Stakes
Sports.content:
It’s day two of the Boodles May Festival, with a whole host of superstars lining up for the Ormonde and Dee Stakes contests.

3.05 Chester - Last year's hero Illinois faces Jan Brueghel

Last year's winner Illinois takes on stablemate Jan Brueghel in a stellar renewal of this Group 3 Ladbrokes Ormonde Stakes.

Aidan O'Brien's 2024 St Leger winner Jan Brueghel took the notable scalp of Calandagan, having outbattled that rival in the Group 1 Coronation Cup at Epsom last June. He failed to confirm the form when only fourth in the King George next time and returns with a bit to prove under Ryan Moore. This is viewed as a prep for Epsom again and he should be monitored in the market.

Illinois, a neck second behind Jan Breughel in the aforementioned St Leger as a three-year-old, made a successful return in this race last season before chasing home Trawlerman in the Gold Cup at Royal Ascot. A dual Group 2 scorer, he is a high-class horse on his day and rates the main danger to his stablemate.

Red Sea Turf Handicap victor Sons And Lovers carries a 5lb penalty, while Karl Burke's Al Qareem has each-way chances given he has the fitness edge on his side.

2.35 Chester - Classy Constitution River fancied for O'Brien

Constitution River headlines a field of six for the Listed Boodles Raindance Dee Stakes at 2.35pm.

Aidan O'Brien has claimed this prize in seven of the last eight years and this son of Wootton Bassett will be popular under Ryan Moore. A narrow second on debut to Tattersalls Stakes winner Distant Storm on debut, he stepped forward to win comfortably at Galway, but it was his Group 2 success at Curragh that marked him down as a potential top-notcher. A decisive winner on that occasion, the step up to 10 furlongs is expected to suit and he may be one for the French Derby.

Image: Constitution River (left) represents Aidan O'Brien

Second-string Flushing Meadows cannot be dismissed under Wayne Lordan. Another son of Wootton Bassett, he was beaten over seven furlongs on his return at Leopardstown and may do better over this extra distance.

Morshdi has a penalty for his Listed Feilden Stakes victory on reappearance at Newmarket and warrants plenty of respect for William Haggas and Tom Marquand. The form has suffered a knock but this lightly raced type ought to progress with racing.

3.40 Chester - Boughey pair McMurray and Moonfall headline

George Boughey holds the aces as he saddles Moonfall and McMurray in a competitive edition of this Xenon Workplace Handicap.

McMurray got off the mark at the third attempt in a Ffos Las maiden in August and has gone from strength to strength since. Stepped up to a mile, he narrowly scored on handicap debut at Doncaster before completing the hat-trick in a two-runner race at Yarmouth. Up another 2lbs, he has a fair draw in stall five and looks like one to follow this summer.

Stablemate Moonfall has undergone a gelding operation since disappointing in the Superlative but beat a useful yardstick when landing a Newbury novice in June and Ryan Moore is a notable booking on this handicap debut.

Of the others, Archer Royal may leave his reappearance behind him, while Factual has won two of his three starts and remains capable of better on this first start in a handicap.

Best of the rest

Roman Dragon boasts three victories around Chester and will be looking to add a fourth when he represents Hugo Palmer in the opening CAA Stellar Handicap at 1.30pm. The Manor House Stables handler also saddles Stratusnine, who chased home Fast Track Harry at Newcastle the last day. Despite showing inconsistencies of late, Seven Questions has been the subject of early market support for Robert Cowell.

Paper View and Donegal Rose are sure to be popular in the market for the 2.05pm British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes before Harvey takes on Londoner in a competitive renewal of the Halliwell Jones Handicap at 4.10pm.

Elsewhere, James Doyle heads to Southwell to ride the Wathnan Racing-owned Enchant in the 8.30pm Follow @attheraces On X Fillies' Novice Stakes. Karl Burke's filly made a winning debut at Pontefract recently and could well go in again.

Internationally, all eyes will be on ParisLongchamp at 3.38pm when Erdenali - who showed a breathtaking turn of foot on debut for Francis-Henri Graffard - returns in the Prix Des Tertres.

Sports.title: Khadija Shaw to leave Manchester City with Chelsea favourites to seal deal
Sports.content:
Khadija “Bunny” Shaw has decided to leave Manchester City this summer at the end of her contract, the Guardian understands, after extensive talks over a new deal concluded with her opting to pursue a new challenge.

The Jamaica striker, who is on course to win the Women’s Super League’s Golden Boot for a third consecutive season, was close to agreeing a new deal in March and is understood to have told City she wanted to stay, but negotiations on the finer details hit a number of stumbling blocks, including the proposed length of the extension, and the WSL leaders are preparing for life without their star player.

Shaw has scored 19 times in 21 WSL games this season to help Manchester City win a first WSL title in 10 years, and is immensely popular with their fans. City and Shaw are understood to be sad about the decision.

Sources have indicated that City were not able to match terms offered by rival teams. Chelsea, reportedly ready to pay Shaw £1m a year, will be the favourites to sign the 29-year-old, who is understood to have attracted interest from many of the world’s biggest clubs, including Barcelona and several NWSL teams. The cash-rich WSL club London City Lionesses are also keen.

Shaw is in line to face Chelsea in Sunday’s Women’s FA Cup semi-final at Stamford Bridge. The following Saturday City play their final league game, at West Ham, having been confirmed as champions on Wednesday night when Arsenal were held to a draw at Brighton.

Shaw is understood to have wanted to avoid speculation affecting City’s pursuit of trophies and conversations about the former Bordeaux player’s future have kept as private as possible.

Shaw, widely recognised as the world’s most in-form central striker, was the Professional Footballers’ Association’s women’s players’ player of the year and the WSL’s player of the season for 2023-24.

Sports.title: Bev Priestman: ‘You become very isolated so I’ve loved getting back on the pitch’
Sports.content:
Football is not the kind of profession that lends itself to time off for birthdays and the like. Especially when one is preparing to lead the Wellington Phoenix into their first A-League Women’s finals campaign, as Bev Priestman was last week. Yet, especially when contrasted with the year prior, when she was still in the midst of a one-year Fifa ban after the spying scandal that engulfed Canada women’s football team during the Paris Olympics, being among “her people” turned out to be a gift in and of itself.

“It was my 40th birthday [last week],” Priestman tells Moving the Goalposts. “And it’s those moments, I think to a year ago, and how I felt. And then how I felt in the club [this year], around my staff, around the team. I do this job because I love people. I love the game, obviously, but it’s working with people, getting your energy with people, and trying to inspire people and help them find a better version of themselves.

“What happened in Paris, and off the back of that, and the media runaway stories that you know necessarily aren’t accurate. You just become very isolated, very, very quickly in a job where it is about being part of a team. That isolation hits you really, really hard, as well as things playing out in the public domain. The biggest joy I’ve had the most this year is just again, getting back on the pitch, working with people who want to be better. I’ve loved that.”

Now, if one were looking for somewhere to make a fresh start, somewhere well off the beaten track away from the spotlight, then Wellington would be right up there. Half a day’s flying from anywhere that isn’t Australia (and even then you’ve got a 10-hour flight to play Perth Glory), its Phoenix are the only professional women’s football team in New Zealand, meaning that it plays in the Australian top-tier.

View image in fullscreen ‘The biggest joy I’ve had the most this year is just again, getting back on the pitch, working with people who want to be better.’ Bev Priestman speaks to her Wellington Phoenix players during a training session. Photograph: Hagen Hopkins/The Guardian

Introduced during the buildup to the Australia and New Zealand co-hosted 2023 Women’s World Cup, they had never reached the end-of-season playoffs in their four campaigns before 2025-26, with their best finish coming in 2023–24, when they finished eighth. They were somewhat lovable losers, generating little in the way of ill-well but rarely threatening to upset the established order.

But in 2025-26, Priestman took the foundation that had been built and constructed perhaps the competition’s most well-oiled machine: fielding its highest scoring attack and most miserly defence, while being among the competition’s leaders in most of its underlying metrics. Under her tutelage, the likes of Brooke Nunn and Grace Jale had breakout campaigns, while the 17-year-old Pia Vlok cemented herself as a star of the future.

This was not enough to break the dynastic hold that Melbourne City – part of the City Football Group – holds over the A-League, but it did secure them a second-place finish and a week off in the first week of the finals. If they can overturn a 2-1 deficit to Brisbane Roar in the second-leg of their semi-final this Sunday, temporary seating brought in to host an expected 5,000-strong crowd at Porirua Park in the biggest game in the team’s history, they will qualify for a first grand final. Needless to say, people have taken notice.

“For the last three months, wherever I go in the city, people seem to know who I am, who the team is, and how we did on the weekend,” Priestman says. “That’s very different to when I arrived in Wellington. It’s really turned into a women’s football community. There’s a buzz about the city. But I think also being the only New Zealand team to compete in the A-League, it’s wider than just Wellington. We’ve got a lot of Football Ferns [New Zealand internationals]. I think there’s a real buzz and energy.”

View image in fullscreen ‘Wherever I go in the city, people seem to know who I am, who the team is, and how we did on the weekend. That’s very different to when I arrived in Wellington.’ Bev Priestman during a Wellington Phoenix team huddle. Photograph: Hagen Hopkins/The Guardian

That Priestman is getting stopped by well-wishers on the street creates a contrast, too, given that she previously spoke about how she “didn’t feel safe” in the aftermath of the spying scandal. New Zealand had always been something of a home, anyway, and her wife, Emma Humphries, was born in Wellington and took up a position as Phoenix’s academy director before the club’s senior women’s role opened up.

“That’s nice. Not to be talked about, maybe for the controversial side of it, and just getting back to what I love and what I know I can be good at, that’s really nice,” she reflects. “And I think it’s the reason you do want to take people with you, to see a bigger opportunity in what you’re doing. And I hope the people at the club, as well, now really do see what women’s football can do.”
